newsitem.title: USA: Texas governor calls for tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Texas governor calls for tax cut.

text.p: Texas Gov. George W. Bush on Tuesday proposed a 40 percent cut in school property taxes, but said other taxes would have to be raised to keep the budget balanced.

Bush, speaking to the Texas Legislature, said the property tax cut would be balanced by a sales tax increase and a broadbased business tax. He also said he would recommend cutting $1 billion from the state budget.
"Property taxes are threatening the Texas dream," he said, adding that homeowners were being taxed beyond their ability to pay.

The Bush plan, which must be approved by the legislature, calls for an increase in the homestead tax exemption from the current $5,000 to $25,000 and a 20 cent cut in school tax rates across the state, which he said would bring the average homeowner a 40 percent tax cut.
But Bush said he would also seek a half cent increase in the state sales tax, half cent increase in the motor vehicle tax and a tax on business sales above $500,000.
The business tax would replace the current corporate franchise tax, which Bush said was inequitable.
He said his new business tax was "capital friendly and will encourage job creation," but he did not say how much money it would raise.
Currently, Texas schools are funded primarily by property taxes levied by local school districts, not by the state.
Bush said all revenues from the new taxes, plus all proceeds from the state lottery, would be placed in a new school trust fund that would become the primary funder of schools.

He said the change would guarantee equitable school financing across the state and help avoid lawsuits from poorer districts who say their students are getting an education equal to the those living in wealthy areas.

Bush said his plan would also "guard against property tax creep" but did not outline how it would do so. Last week, he told reporters he would propose that all future school tax increases be put before the voters for approval.
